---
title: "Computational Algebraic Topology from Scratch"
subtitle: "A constructive path from elementary topology to persistent homology"
toc: true
---

These notes develop computational algebraic topology from first principles.
They are intended for readers with undergraduate linear algebra and some
mathematical maturity, but no prior knowledge of algebraic topology.

The central idea is to turn geometric and topological questions into finite
algebraic computations. In particular, we will study why

$$
\partial_k \circ \partial_{k+1}=0
$$

and how this identity leads to homology groups, algorithms, filtrations, and
persistent homology.

## Planned structure

1. Mathematical prerequisites
2. Topological spaces and continuity
3. Simplicial and cubical complexes
4. Groups, vector spaces, and chain complexes
5. Homology
6. Boundary matrices and reduction algorithms
7. Filtrations and persistence modules
8. Stability
9. Implementations and worked examples

## Status

These notes are under development. Chapters will be added and revised
incrementally.
